TL;DR - A security guard named Paul, an old Vietnam vet who liked dirty jokes and giving advice, was reported by his peer Shannon, as I inadvertently and nonchalantly chatted about that one time Paul almost dozed off for the hotel's inactivity. Shannon had showed me a gun and dropped it, even though she was not aloud to have one, so I asked Voat how to approach the vengeance of Paul.

Paul was supposed to come in tonight but instead another female guard appeared. I asked her if Paul was around and she said she didn't know him. I told her about what happened and she confirmed that he may have been fired, hence her presence.

I'm writing a letter to the supervisor. Here's what it says:

This is a formal complaint to be given to the supervisor of [security outfit] over the [hotel]. This regards the security guard named Shannon. I would like to inform the supervisor that Shannon, against rules and regulations, had at one time shown myself, an attendant at the [hotel], a weapon which she claimed she should not have had in the first place. I was not on the clock, and it was not in the presence of any guests; in fact it was only herself and I involved. In the process of pulling the weapon out she fumbled it and it fell to the floor. I do not know if it was armed, but had it been, there may have been a possibility that it discharged a round. This behavior is highly inappropriate, and it made me feel confused and astonished that a guard would disregard the precautions taken to ensure a safe and stable environment, as that is their job to begin with. I do hope the proper measures are taken as reprehension against the individual.

On one hand Paul was far too old to be a guard fit for duty in case something did happen, but on the other he only needed this job for a year before he would possibly attain his full veteran's disability comp. And then there's the fact that a friend of mine got another friend fired over this. Paul was a great man and he did not do a damn thing to me to deserve this. I still do feel responsible. But on the other hand Shannon sacrificed an old and innocent man in hopes that she would get something out of it.

I should see the supervisor soon. I am actually leaving the employment of my hotel by August 1st and I think I should hand this in then, to prevent any sort of unforeseen consequences. For all I know Shannon could be fired and she would have it in for me, and she knows where I work. If this letter has little potential for that by the time I leave then I will hand it in now, but if it does have potential I will wait. I need your opinions again Voat. You pushed me to exact justice, I just need advice on the timing.

Edit: Nevermind, I had told the supervisor that I had a complaint to file, and even though I was on the fence to give it out, there was no point in waiting. I handed it in to him. So we'll see what happens.

I think easing him into a different job would have been better, but, I'll leave that decision to those in charge.
